latest.text: Good afternoon. This is a synthetic test matter. We act for Aster Fabrication in Hyderabad. Our client rented a precision cutter and says it returned the machine on 6 September 2026. The owner retains the Rs 1,20,000 security deposit, alleging damage to the cutting head; our client denies causing damage. The owner sent a technician's estimate but no joint inspection report. Our client reports having a signed hire agreement and a bank-transfer receipt, but I have not supplied or examined those documents here. Separately, the owner's technician still has our client's original design drive, which the client says was lent only for setup; the owner now says it can retain the drive until repair costs are paid. First give a source-backed, conditional analysis of the deposit and drive disputes, including any material contrary position. Separately, draft a brief list of questions for our client that would clarify the important gaps. Do not contact anyone, do not treat the damage allegation as admitted, and do not assume the reported documents have been checked.

observations.title: Union Of India 2023 2 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
observations.reason: The complete supplied passage states a general burden-of-proof proposition. It is pertinent to investigating the disputed allegation and proof, but it does not decide the specific deposit or drive dispute. Its applicable version, procedure and source authenticity remain unassessed. This is new lexical recall outside the fused 60, so adding this route alone would still not supply this source downstream.
observations.exact_text:
Union Of India 2023 2 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023,  — s.105: On whom burden of proof lies.
105.
On whom burden of proof lies.
The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side.
Illustrations.
(a) A sues B for land of which B is in possession, and which, as A asserts, was left to A by the will of C, B's father. If no evidence were given on either side, B would be entitled to retain his possession. Therefore, the burden of proof is on A.
(b) A sues B for money due on a bond. The execution of the bond is admitted, but B says that it was obtained by fraud, which A denies. If no evidence were given on either side, A would succeed, as the bond is not disputed and the fraud is not proved. Therefore, the burden of proof is on B.

observations.title: Union Of India 1965 3 Bar Council Of India Rules
observations.reason: This rule addresses an advocate becoming a witness. The supplied account concerns a client's equipment and property; the passage does not support its substantive disputes merely because it mentions an advocate and client.
observations.exact_text:
Union Of India 1965 3 Bar Council Of India Rules,  — s.13: An Advocate should not accept a brief or appear in a case in which he has reason to believe that he will be a witness, and if being engaged in a case, it becomes apparent that he is a witness on a material question of fact, he should not continue to appear as an Advocate if he can retire without jeopardising his client 's interests.

conclusion: Independent original-account retrieval adds a distinct recall route, including limited useful leads absent from the legal-enquiry raw legs. It also adds extensive wrong-scope, account-only and contaminated material. No evidence supports promoting the route directly into final answer support or substituting it for legal enquiry retrieval.
mechanism_findings: A useful general evidence provision enters only the new lexical leg but falls outside the unchanged 60-result per-query fusion cutoff. An added route does not ensure it survives to ranking.

Factual vocabulary can find machinery-related judicial discussion absent from legal-enquiry pools, while advocate/client and equipment vocabulary also retrieves professional rules, forms and unrelated schemes.
Some results are allegations or recounted arbitral decisions; rhetorical role and precise source purpose must remain independent from candidate relevance.
New position counts are not new legal propositions; duplicated instruments, parent/child overlap and already available context must be reconciled separately.
remaining_limits: The original live run did not save raw work-pool ranks. These are reconstructed from its exact admitted queries under matching current corpus revisions; only final/context evidence is an actual saved result.
The held drive work was not silently restored; no completion or legal-applicability claim follows from this experiment.
No parent mapping, final reranking, complete-judgment reading, source currency verification or browser answer was executed.
One already-seen synthetic matter, one execution, no control for warm-cache latency and no precision/recall denominator.
No production changes or scenario-based search exclusions were introduced. No second matter or further search was run.
